messages:
incident-bot: Pager: elevated 5xx rate detected for tenant QuasarRetail on Dedicated cluster ded-eu-4. 5xx rate 18% over 5m, p95 latency 2.8s. Auto-escalation to #incidents. Incident ID: INC-20260315-8342. Link: https://console.redwood/incidents/INC-2026/8342

oncall-amy: I'm on it. Paging runtime and infra.

mike-sre: I'm looking at cluster ded-eu-4 now. Seeing GPU mem pressure on node gpu-12 and repeated model restarts. Example logs:
```
2026-03-15T12:34:56Z model-server[pid=2222]: ERROR: eviction triggered, kv-cache miss flood, OOM when allocating 12.3GB
2026-03-15T12:35:02Z nginx: 502 upstream reset while reading response header from upstream
```

julia-eng-runtime: Noting lots of long-sequence requests from tenant quasar (bursting). Their batch size seems very high. Query from our metrics: tenant_quasar -> avg tokens per request 4200, concurrency spiking.

sara-cs: QuasarRetail monitoring shows customer-side alerts about partial failures in checkout flows. Business impact: ~7% of sessions seeing error page.

mike-sre: Running `redwoodctl cluster nodes --cluster ded-eu-4 --filter gpu-12` -> shows 94% memory and 98% GPU util. Also `kubectl get pods -n serving -o wide | grep quasar` shows 3 pods pinned to gpu-12 with restarts.

julia-eng-runtime: Suggest immediate mitigation: soft-evict noisy tenant traffic onto spare pool ded-eu-4-burst or throttle concurrency for tenant quasar.

oncall-amy: Initiating traffic shift. @deploy-bot, can we create a temporary routing-rule to route tenant=quasar to ded-eu-4-burst and cap concurrency to 4? :pray:

deploy-bot: Creating route rule... done. Applied concurrency cap=4 for tenant quasar. Rolling out in 12s.

mike-sre: Observing drop in 5xx from 18% -> 6% within 40s. Node gpu-12 mem pressure easing. Starting graceful drain of one pod causing restarts.

julia-eng-runtime: Also pushed a quick quantized model variant for quasar to reduce memory. rollout id: rr-20260315-01. Canary on 1 pod.

sara-cs: Confirmed with QuasarRetail that they see reduced errors now. They will keep monitoring.

oncall-amy: Keeping this in incident state until stable p95 < 1s and 5xx <1% for 10m. Assigning follow-ups: eng-runtime to investigate token limits and per-tenant batching; infra to add node-level auto-eviction thresholds.

mike-sre: Note: the root cause appears to be tenant sending very long requests and large batch parallelism causing KV cache thrash and memory OOMs -> cascade to 502/504.

julia-eng-runtime: Agreed. Action items: enforce per-tenant max_seq_length in routing, expose tenant-specific batching knob to customers, and add metric alert for kv-cache miss rate.

sara-cs: Logged customer impact and agreed to offer credits if required. CC @account-exec-lina.

oncall-amy: Closing incident. Resolved at 1778890899. Summary saved to incident tracker INC-20260315-8342. Thanks all :tada:

deploy-bot: Incident channel auto-archived.
